summary: Readability is high for the surrounding doctrine + walkthrough docs, but the ADR prose itself sits at a senior-engineer baseline. A programming-capable intern with no hyperscaler background can follow the intern-walkthrough end-to-end and the day-one runbook with minimal stumbles, and the reading-order doc provides excellent scaffolding. However, the ADRs themselves (especially 0243, 0248, 0255, 0257, 0292) routinely introduce ~12-18 jargon terms per page before defining them, lean heavily on inline references (ADR-XXXX D-N) without inline gloss, and assume reader familiarity with industry references (Stripe Brandur post, Hamilton 2007 LISA paper, MacCarthaigh shuffle-sharding article, AWS Builder's Library, James Hamilton principles) as load-bearing context rather than optional. The intern-walkthrough successfully ties everything together, but only because it does the glossing the ADRs declined to do. Sentences are clear and well-punctuated; structure is consistent across ADRs (Status / Date / Context / Decision / Consequences). The biggest readability cliffs are: (a) bare CamelCase / dotted-scope identifiers introduced without expansion (e.g., `oyatie.foundry.ci-agent`, `SPIFFE SVID`, `ML-KEM-768`, `HLC`, `BNF v4.1`, `NFKC`); (b) inline statute citations (FRCP 37(e), Sedona Working Group 1, UTS#36, FTC COPPA Rule, CT logs, RFC 9420) without one-line gloss; (c) dense markdown tables that intern eyes parse as walls; (d) keystone cross-references (`ADR-0243 D-3 catalogue`) that require the intern to open three files in parallel to follow a single decision. The intern-walkthrough partially compensates by glossing on the spot, and the day-one runbook does an excellent job of inline-defining terms as they appear in commands. Net: the bundle is buildable by an intern who reads the reading-order + walkthrough + day-one runbook first, then the ADRs second. Reverse order would defeat them.

strengths: Clear thesis statement in frontmatter `purpose` block.
Context section's 'What every named hyperscaler reference actually does' bullet list is genuinely useful and intern-readable.
D-1 reserved-namespace rationale is well-justified with concrete homograph examples.
Bootstrap sequence table (D-5) is a model of clarity: stepwise, each step explains why it depends on the previous.
weaknesses: Frontmatter has 16 amends/related/related_specs/related_memory keys that an intern cannot evaluate; recommend a 'tldr' or 'intern_entry_point' field.
`advisory-until-tenant-bootstrap-lands` is used as a load-bearing term without inline definition; intern must infer from context.
`audience-as-microservice-scope framing` is jargon for a concept from superseded ADRs; needs a one-line gloss.
DSAR is used in D-4 before being fully expanded inline.
Sub-scope patterns `oyatie.cell.<cell-id>` and `oyatie.preview.<pr-number>` are presented without explaining their functional differences.

strengths: 23-row policy-class table in Context is the bundle's best teaching artifact — concrete, exhaustive, gives intern an immediate mental model of why the doctrine exists.
'What this is NOT' section is a model of doctrine clarity.
D-3 minimum-required gate set table is intern-readable.
weaknesses: `Cedar`, `Kyverno`, `OPA`, `SCP`, `IAM`, `Verified Permissions` used in Context without one-line gloss; intern who has never touched AWS must Google all of them.
`finite-time decidable`, `Turing-complete policies`, `union-with-tie-break-by-deny` lose interns without compiler-theory background.
Eight-state fragment lifecycle (authored → reviewed → signed → published → activated → in-force → sunset → tombstoned) is listed, not diagrammed.
Cedar evaluation contract code block (Rust) at D-1 uses Rust standard library types without gloss; JS/Python-background intern stumbles.
D-6 performance budgets table buries the lede: 1ms p99 hot-path target appears as a row, not as a thesis.

strengths: 'James Hamilton's 2007 LISA paper' Context section is well-paced and tells the historical story clearly.
MacCarthaigh shuffle sharding math (`P(full overlap) = 1 / C(100, 8) ≈ 5.4 × 10^-12`) is correctly explained.
Pre-ADR-0248 deployment topology section is intern-readable: five-bullet list of what was broken before.
weaknesses: Hamilton's eighteen principles cited by number — intern needs to either trust the quoting or read a 2007 paper.
`Borg`, `Omega`, `Pingora`, `Brad Calder ARC408`, `Becky Weiss + Mike Furr` — author/talk citations intern cannot fact-check without external access.
Tier 0 list (D-1) uses `GitHub`, `Harbor`, `cert-manager`, `SPIFFE/SPIRE`, `Cilium-ambient`, `Kata Containers`, `Cloud Hypervisor` without inline gloss.
Per-tier table is referenced (D-7, D-11, D-12) but requires non-trivial chasing across sub-sections.

Cellular blast-radius mathematical claim is presented without graceful-degradation framing — an intern might wonder 'why 8% degradation across all tenants is preferable to 1% full outage' without the AWS Builder's Library context.

strengths: 'What ADR-0220 said (and where it broke)' Context narrative is excellent prose; tells a story rather than lists rules.
Two-layer ASCII diagram (D-1) helps visualize the substrate/brand-surface split.
D-2 + D-3 BC tables (8 substrate + 6 consumer surface) are clearly enumerated with crate names + responsibilities.
weaknesses: `BC` (Bounded Context) used heavily without inline expansion on first use; intern with no DDD background stumbles.

Provider list (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Cohere, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, vLLM-self-hosted, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Apple Foundation Models API, OpenRouter, Together, Groq) uses provider-specific shorthand.
BYOK is in the title and D-4 — finally expanded as 'Bring Your Own Key' inline in D-4, but interns scanning frontmatter see acronyms unmoored.
`MCP servers per Anthropic Model Context Protocol 2024` — intern is told to consume MCP without being told what MCP is.
Audience-tag table is excellent BUT presumes intern already understands the `oyatie.*` principal naming scheme from ADR-0242 D-2.
`caller-side RAG` used without inline gloss; intern needs to know what RAG is and what 'caller-side' means here.

strengths: F-MISSED-2 callout (the Palantir Tectonic story) is a memorable, intern-readable cautionary tale.
Three named-patterns block (Stripe API versioning / Palantir SchemaRevision / Protobuf+Avro) walks through industry convergence cleanly.
SemVer 2.0.0 is reintroduced inline — good move for intern accessibility.
weaknesses: `Tier-1 lockdown bundle` is presented as if intern already knows what Tier-1 lockdowns are; needs a one-line bridge sentence on first appearance.
Failure modes 1-6 in Context — #5 (`agent-gateway tool-spec drift`) assumes intern knows what tool-call protocol and LLM tool-spec caching are.
Brandur Leach 'APIs as ladders' is cited but not linked; intern reading offline cannot follow.
Handshake state machine (ACTIVE → DEPRECATED → TOMBSTONED) is named in Status but mechanics live deep in §D — intern may not connect them on a first read.
`buf.build/docs/breaking/rules` referenced as canonical without sample rules; intern is sent to a URL.

per_adr_findings.adr: ADR-0292 (Minor User Doctrine — COPPA + KOSA + EU Age Verification)
strengths: Penalty matrix table (Context) is the bundle's most directly accessible business-impact teaching — intern sees USD 50,120 per child and immediately understands stakes.
Per-jurisdiction breakdown is concrete and dated (FTC TikTok 5.7M, YouTube 170M, Epic 275M, etc.).

Hyperscaler reference list (Apple Family Sharing, Google Family Link, Microsoft Family Safety, Meta Teen Accounts, TikTok For You, Roblox, Discord Teen Safety Assist, Snap Family Center) gives intern a map of the industry.
weaknesses: Acronyms COPPA, KOSA, AADC, PIPA, FSS, METI, MOGEF, KCC, eSafety, OOSA, DSA, DPA, EDPB, FERPA, FRCP, BAA, DPIA introduced as if intern already knows them — only some expanded inline.
`tenant.facing ∈ { B2C, B2B2C, B2C2B }` uses set-membership notation intern without set-theory exposure may stumble on.
Korean/Japanese statute citations appear without romanization or English-only fallback — intern who reads neither language sees opaque ideographs.
Six enforcement preconditions in Status are dense; would benefit from a numbered checklist with explicit owner per item.
`MINOR-USER-2024 pack` referenced before being defined; intern who reads top-down learns the name before learning what it contains.
`parens patriae state actions` (US legal doctrine) used without gloss.

intern_buildability_rationale: An intern who reads in the order specified by /docs/architecture/keystone-bundle-reading-order.md (Phase 0 reading-order doc; Phase 1 ADRs 0242, 0243, 0244, 0245; etc.) and the day-one runbook can absolutely build the bootstrap substrate locally and ship a first PR. The reading-order doc budgets 21-32 hours explicitly, gives self-check questions per phase, and the day-one runbook has step-by-step commands with acceptance criteria + 15 common errors. The intern-walkthrough (Alice's MLS DM) is an excellent canonical worked example. However, an intern who skips the reading-order and starts with ADRs directly will stall within 30-45 minutes because the ADRs do not gloss their own jargon. PARTIAL because buildability is high WITH the support docs and LOW without them; the bundle's readability is therefore a function of reading-order discipline, which the docs do enforce but the ADRs themselves do not signpost.

ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: Reader does not know if 'advisory' means 'validators run but never fail CI' or 'validators do not run at all'. Next paragraph clarifies but first sentence is ambiguous in isolation.

ambiguous_passages.passage: The SDK falls back to in-µservice cached decision if the cell-local evaluator is unreachable for ≥ 200 ms
ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: Is 200ms a circuit-breaker timeout per request, a cumulative window, or an SLO observation? Intern parsing fast cannot tell.

ambiguous_passages.passage: (S/C) × C / S = 100% of tenants experience some degradation
ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: Algebra simplifies to 1 (100% of tenants), correct but presented opaquely. Intern sees the math but not the intuition (every tenant has some affected shard but only 1/S of their shards).

ambiguous_passages.passage: Both layers ship from the same Cargo workspace (`microservices/intelligence/`) but are distinct Cargo crates per BC.
ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: Intern: does a Cargo workspace correspond to a µservice or to a deployable unit? Per the rest of the bundle these are 1:1, but the sentence does not say so explicitly.

ambiguous_passages.passage: any tenant whose `tenant.facing ∈ { B2C, B2B2C, B2C2B }`
ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: `tenant.facing` versus `tenant.audience_type` — two field names appear in adjacent ADRs (0244 introduces `audience_type`, 0292 uses `tenant.facing`). Intern cannot tell if synonyms or distinct.

ambiguous_passages.passage: The 2026-05-19 idea-refine session that produced this Tier-1 lockdown bundle surfaced 'Ontology Object-Type Versioning + Deprecation Handshake' as F-MISSED-2
ambiguous_passages.ambiguity: F-MISSED-2 is jargon for a meta-process; intern is told the ADR exists because of a process artifact they have not seen.

recommendations.recommendation: Add a one-paragraph 'For interns' inline-gloss block at the top of each ADR (after `purpose`, before `Status`) expanding the 6-10 most jargon-heavy terms on that page. Cross-link to day-one runbook glossary §12.

Add a sentinel acronym-expansion table to the front of the reading-order doc covering the union of all acronyms in the 14-ADR bundle. Day-one runbook §12 carries a glossary, but reading-order Phase 0 does not — and interns hit ADRs first.
Disambiguate `audience_type` (ADR-0244) vs `tenant.facing` (ADR-0292); pick one canonical field name and let CI enforce it.
Convert ADR-0243 D-2 fragment lifecycle from list to explicit Mermaid or ASCII state-machine diagram; intern eye traversal of state machines is dramatically faster as a diagram.

Add romanized + English-glossed citation form to non-Latin statute references in ADR-0292. Example: `KR Youth Protection Revision Act 2024 (Korean: 청소년 보호법 개정, romanized: Cheongsonyeon Boho-beop Gaejeong)`.
Surround inline statute citations (FRCP 37(e), UTS#39, RFC 9420, GDPR Article 17, FTC COPPA Rule §312.5(b), CACM 2016, KR-FSS) with a footnote-style one-line description on first appearance per ADR.
Intern-walkthrough §1.1/§1.2 tables use `dr_cell`, `home_cell`, `compliance_packs_active`, `sovereign_cloud_pack`, `dr_tier` as keys without expansion. Add a glossary-inline column or leading legend.
Standardize ADR cross-reference format. Bundle mixes `ADR-0243 D-3 catalogue`, `ADR-0243 §D-3`, `ADR-0243 D-3`, and `ADR-0243 §D-3 catalogue`. Pick one form.
Reading-order doc §5.1 (Phase 1 self-check) is excellent. Apply same pattern to ADRs themselves: each ADR ends with 3-4 self-check questions intern can answer to verify comprehension.

structural_consistency_assessment.frontmatter_uniformity: GOOD — all ADRs in the bundle carry frontmatter with id/status/date/owners/supersedes/amends/related/related_specs/related_memory/doc_class/keystone_bundle/keystone_position/purpose/enforcement_status/enforced_by. Schema is uniform.
structural_consistency_assessment.section_ordering: GOOD — Status → Date → Context → Decision → Consequences consistent across the bundle.
structural_consistency_assessment.decision_section_granularity: MIXED — some ADRs use D-1..D-N sequentially; others mix D-N with sub-headings that look like sub-sections but are actually top-level Decision items. Intern parses inconsistency.
structural_consistency_assessment.table_use: GOOD — most ADRs use tables for enumerable lists; intern eye finds them quickly.
structural_consistency_assessment.code_block_balance: MIXED — Rust code blocks in ADR-0242 D-6 and ADR-0255 D-4 are intern-readable for Rustaceans; Python/JS interns may stumble. Recommend pseudocode alternative or inline gloss of Rust type signatures.
structural_consistency_assessment.ascii_diagram_use: PARTIAL — ADR-0255 D-1 has a single ASCII diagram. ADR-0248 (which would benefit most from a four-tier topology diagram) does not include one in the read portion.

intern_walkthrough_assessment.tldr_quality: EXCELLENT — opening callout block ('Read this once and you understand the platform') sets clear expectations.
intern_walkthrough_assessment.section_structure: EXCELLENT — six sections explicitly enumerated in §0; conventions block explains tenant ID format, cell naming, Cedar gate citation form, HLC notation.
intern_walkthrough_assessment.step_density: 70+ numbered steps with consistent (Source / What happens / Why it matters architecturally) triple. The 'Why it matters architecturally' field is the document's secret weapon.
intern_walkthrough_assessment.citation_quality: HIGH — every step cites the specific ADR § / PRD § / standard § that governs it.
intern_walkthrough_assessment.intern_buildability_through_walkthrough: YES — an intern can absolutely follow Alice's MLS DM end-to-end and recompose the architecture. The walkthrough does the glossing the ADRs do not.
weaknesses: Conventions block §0 covers HLC and SPIFFE briefly but does not gloss MLS, AAD, AEAD, SeaweedFS, tus.io, APNs upfront.
Steps past §54 (Phase G/H + failure scenarios + comparator section) not visible in the read excerpt.

reading_order_assessment.phase_structure: EXCELLENT — nine phases with time budgets, reading goals, self-check questions per phase.
reading_order_assessment.scaffolding_quality: EXCELLENT — explicit prerequisites block (§2) plus explicit 'concepts you do not need yet' (§2.3).
reading_order_assessment.self_check_quality: GOOD — 20-question quiz at §13 with answer key location at §13.3.
reading_order_assessment.common_confusions_section: EXCELLENT — §14 addresses exactly the questions an intern would actually ask.
weaknesses: §14 confusion answers do not have backwards-pointers to where the canonical answer lives in the ADR.
Reading-order doc does NOT carry a glossary; relies on day-one runbook §12. Phase 0 readers may not encounter the glossary until day-one runbook phase.

day_one_runbook_assessment.scope_clarity: EXCELLENT — §2.1 explicitly enumerates in-scope and out-of-scope items.
day_one_runbook_assessment.step_structure: EXCELLENT — each of 10 steps has Goal / Procedure / Acceptance / Common gotchas.
day_one_runbook_assessment.error_recovery: EXCELLENT — §7 lists top 15 likely first-day errors with diagnosis + fix.
day_one_runbook_assessment.glossary_quality: EXCELLENT — §12 covers 30+ canonical terms with cross-link to defining ADR/spec.
day_one_runbook_assessment.escalation_chain: EXCELLENT — §8 four-tier escalation with concrete file paths.
day_one_runbook_assessment.intern_buildability_through_runbook: YES — an intern who reads Phase 1 of reading-order and then follows day-one runbook can absolutely complete day one. Runbook + reading-order pair is the single most important readability artifact in the bundle.
weaknesses: Step 5 assumes the Helm chart at `microservices/tenancy/charts/tenancy/` exists as a complete chart; runbook does not warn intern what to do if chart is in-flight or scaffolded.
Common error 7.11 requires intern to know what UTS#39 confusable removal is — runbook explains but does not link out to UTS#39.
Acceptance criterion §5 item 10 depends on multispectrum review pipeline being live — runbook does not say how to proceed if review is unavailable.

go_with_fixes_summary: Bundle is shippable from a readability standpoint provided synthesizer requires before merge: (1) add a top-of-ADR 'For interns' jargon-gloss block to ADR-0242, 0243, 0248, 0255, 0257, 0292 (high priority); (2) hoist day-one runbook §12 glossary into reading-order Phase 0 (high priority); (3) reconcile `audience_type` vs `tenant.facing` field naming across ADR-0244 + ADR-0292 (medium priority); (4) convert ADR-0243 D-2 fragment lifecycle list into an explicit state-machine diagram (medium priority); (5) add romanized + English-glossed citation form to non-Latin statute references in ADR-0292 (medium priority). With those five fixes the F3-Readability verdict promotes from WARN to PERMIT. Without them the bundle remains buildable by disciplined interns who follow the reading-order, but stumbles for interns who jump into ADRs directly — which is the realistic agentic-pipeline case where AI agents read ADRs first without the reading-order context.
